newsitem.title: USA: TVA to offer $300 mln in CPI-linked bonds.
newsitem.headline: TVA to offer $300 mln in CPI-linked bonds.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority Tuesday said it became the first U.S. corporation in history to offer inflation-indexed bonds with the sale of $300 million in 10-year securities.
TVA's "Valley Inflation-indexed Power Securities" are designed to meet investors' needs for a hedge against inflation, said TVA Chairman Craven Crowell.
The U.S. Treasury for the first time last week offered an inflation-indexed note, which met with tremendous investor demand.
With an inflation-indexed bond, semi-annual interest payments are based on the inflation-adjusted principal at the time the interest is paid.
"Inflation-indexed bonds represent a new investment opportunity for both individual and institutional investors throughout the world," said TVA Chief Financial Officer David Smith.
Merrill Lynch is the lead manager and sole underwriter for the bond sale. Proceeds from the sale will be used to help retire existing TVA debt.

TVA is the nation's largest producer of electricity and its power system is self-financed. The utility provides power to large industries and 160 power distributors that serve almost eight million consumers in seven southeastern states.
